questions.question_text: Two vectors P = 5î + 2ĵ + 4k̂ and Q = 2î – 5ĵ + 0k̂. The angle between them is:
questions.explanation: Compute the dot product: P · Q = (5)(2) + (2)(−5) + (4)(0) = 10 − 10 + 0 = 0. Since the dot product is zero, cos θ = 0, giving θ = 90°.

questions.question_text: Which of the following vectors is perpendicular to (î + 2ĵ)?
questions.explanation: Checking option (B): Dot product (î + 2ĵ) · (6î − 3ĵ) = (1)(6) + (2)(−3) = 0. Magnitude = √(6² + (−3)²) = √45 = 3√5 units.
questions.formula: Two vectors A and B are perpendicular if A · B = 0

questions.question_text: If the component of vector A along B equals √3 times the component of B along A, what is the ratio A : B?
questions.explanation: Component of A along B is A cos θ; component of B along A is B cos θ. Given A cos θ = √3 (B cos θ), cancelling cos θ gives A/B = √3/1.
questions.formula: Component of A along B = A cos θ
questions.review_note: Verify the original PDF wording for this question — the direction of the equality may differ.

questions.question_text: If A and B are unit vectors, the value of |A − B|² / |A + B|² is:
questions.explanation: Since A and B are unit vectors, |A|=|B|=1 and A·B = cos θ. |A−B|² = 1 − 2cos θ + 1 = 2(1 − cos θ). |A+B|² = 2(1 + cos θ). Using half-angle identities: (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ) = [2 sin²(θ/2)] / [2 cos²(θ/2)] = tan²(θ/2).
questions.review_note: Verify the question asks for |A-B|²/|A+B|² or a related expression.

questions.question_text: A 10 kg object is lifted to a height of 10 m and given a velocity of 2 m/s. The total work done is (g = 9.8 m/s²):
questions.explanation: Total work done = Potential Energy gain + Kinetic Energy gain = mgh + ½mv² = 10(9.8)(10) + ½(10)(2²) = 980 + 20 = 1000 J.

questions.question_text: A bucket filled with water weighing 20 kg is raised from a well of depth 20 m. If the linear density of the rope is 0.2 kg/m, the total work done is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation: Rope mass = 0.2 × 20 = 4 kg. Total work = Work on bucket + Work on rope center of gravity = m_bucket × g × h + m_rope × g × (h/2) = 20(10)(20) + 4(10)(10) = 4000 + 400 = 4400 J.

questions.topic: Work done on a hanging chain
questions.question_text: A uniform chain of length 2 m is kept on a table such that 60 cm hangs freely over the edge. Total mass is 4 kg. Work done in pulling the entire chain onto the table is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation: Hanging length = 0.6 m, total length = 2 m. Hanging fraction = 0.6/2 = 3/10. Mass of hanging part = 4 × (3/10) = 1.2 kg. Center of gravity of hanging part is at 0.3 m below edge. Work W = m_hang × g × (L_hang/2) = 1.2 × 10 × 0.3 = 3.6 J.
questions.review_note: Solution in PDF uses a different formula notation W = mgL/(2n²) — verify both approaches give 3.6 J.

questions.topic: Work done in rearranging a block
questions.question_text: A rectangular block of dimensions 6 m × 4 m × 2 m and density 1.5 g/cm³ lies on horizontal ground with its largest face in contact. Work done in arranging it with its smallest face in contact with ground is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation: Volume V = 6×4×2 = 48 m³, mass m = 48 × 1500 = 72,000 kg. Initial CG height h₁ = 2/2 = 1 m (smallest dimension/2); final CG height h₂ = 6/2 = 3 m (largest dimension/2). W = mg(h₂ − h₁) = 72000 × 10 × (3 − 1) = 1,440,000 J = 1440 kJ.

questions.question_text: A body of mass 5 kg moving along a straight line accelerates from 4 m/s to 8 m/s upon application of a 10 N force. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = F/m = 10/5 = 2 m/s². Time t = (v − u)/a = (8 − 4)/2 = 2 s. Displacement s = (v² − u²)/(2a) = (64 − 16)/4 = 12 m. Work W = F × s = 10 × 12 = 120 J. All statements are true.
questions.formula: a = F/m; t = (v−u)/a; s = (v²−u²)/(2a); W = F·s

questions.question_text: A uniform rod of length 2 m and mass 5 kg lies on a horizontal surface. Work done in raising one end until the rod makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation: Height gained by center of gravity h = (L/2) sin 30° = 1 × 0.5 = 0.5 m. Work done W = mgh = 5 × 10 × 0.5 = 25 J.

questions.question_text: A force of 5 N is applied to a 20 kg mass initially at rest. The work done during the 3rd second of its motion is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = F/m = 5/20 = 0.25 m/s². Distance in 3rd second: S₃ = u + a(2n−1)/2 = 0 + 0.25(2×3−1)/2 = 0.25 × 5/2 = 5/8 m. Work W = F × S₃ = 5 × (5/8) = 25/8 J.

questions.topic: Work done lifting in a fluid
questions.question_text: The work done in lifting a body of mass 20 kg and relative density 3.2 to a height of 8 m in water is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation: Apparent weight = mg(1 − ρ_water/ρ_body) = 20 × 10 × (1 − 1/3.2) = 200 × (2.2/3.2) = 200 × 0.6875 = 137.5 N. Work = Apparent weight × height = 137.5 × 8 = 1100 J.
questions.formula: F_apparent = mg(1 − ρ_liquid/ρ_body); W = F_apparent × h

questions.question_text: A body of mass 3 kg experiences displacement S = t²/3 (in m). Work done by the force in first 2 seconds is:
questions.explanation: Given S = t²/3, velocity v = dS/dt = 2t/3. At t = 0, v₀ = 0; at t = 2, v = 4/3 m/s. By Work-Energy Theorem: W = ½m(v² − u²) = ½(3)((4/3)² − 0) = ½ × 3 × 16/9 = 8/3 J ≈ 2.67 J. NOTE: The PDF solution gives W = ½(3)(4²) = 24 J using v = t² at t=2, which differs from the displacement formula given. This is a discrepancy in the source PDF.
questions.review_note: DISCREPANCY: The PDF question gives S = t²/3 but the solution uses v = t² (implying S = t³/3). The correct answer per the PDF answer key is (D) 24 J, accepting the solution as authoritative. Manual verification of the original PDF required.

When a spring is compressed by 3 cm, stored potential energy is U. When compressed by an additional 3 cm, the increase in potential energy is:
questions.explanation: U₁ = ½k(3)² = 9(½k) = U, so ½k = U/9. For total compression 6 cm: U₂ = ½k(6)² = 36(½k) = 36(U/9) = 4U. Increase ΔU = U₂ − U₁ = 4U − U = 3U.

questions.question_text: If the kinetic energy of a body increases by 125%, the percentage increase in its momentum is:
questions.explanation: New KE = 2.25 × old KE. Since p = √(2mKE), momentum ratio p₂/p₁ = √(KE₂/KE₁) = √2.25 = 1.5. Percentage increase = (1.5 − 1) × 100% = 50%.

questions.topic: Kinetic energy with mass and velocity change
questions.question_text: The kinetic energy of a body is K. If one-fourth of its mass is removed and its velocity is doubled, its new kinetic energy is:
questions.explanation: Remaining mass m' = (3/4)m, new velocity v' = 2v. New KE K' = ½ × (3/4)m × (2v)² = ½ × (3/4)m × 4v² = (3/4)(4) × (½mv²) = 3K.
